record.category: scholarly metadata API (DOI registry) and annual public data file

free_tier.stated: No sign-up: the public pool allows 5 requests a second for a single record and 1 a second for lists of records, 1 at a time; the polite pool, selected by an email address in the mailto parameter or the agent header, allows 10 a second for single DOI records and 3 a second for lists, 3 at a time; no daily cap is published
free_tier.notes: Measured on 2026-10-30: an anonymous list call answered x-rate-limit-limit 1, x-rate-limit-interval 1s, x-concurrency-limit 1 in pool public-array; an anonymous single-DOI call answered x-rate-limit-limit 5 in pool public-single.

per_object_cap.stated: rows default 20, maximum 1000 per call; cursor paging for deeper result sets

retention.stated: the API is a live index; the public data file is released once a year (the 2026 file on 2026 March 17); monthly snapshots for Metadata Plus subscribers stay available until the end of the following quarter

egress.terms: The API is not metered by bytes. The annual public data file is distributed over Academic Torrents; its copy in the S3 bucket api-snapshots-reqpays-crossref is Requester Pays, so the downloader's AWS account pays the transfer, estimated by Crossref at USD 18 for the 2025 file of about 200 GB.
egress.free_allowance: the torrent has no published cap; the Requester Pays copy has no free allowance

record.interface_detail: REST at https://api.crossref.org (works, members, funders, journals; JSON; cursor paging); the annual public data file as gzip JSONL over BitTorrent (Academic Torrents, doi:10.13003/nggf-vt1j) or from the Requester Pays S3 bucket api-snapshots-reqpays-crossref with --request-payer requester; monthly snapshots at https://api.crossref.org/snapshots/monthly/ for Metadata Plus tokens only
record.tooling: curl or any HTTP client for the API; a BitTorrent client for the public data file; aws s3api get-object --request-payer requester for the S3 copy, which needs an AWS account
record.chaining: The annual public data file is the bulk path: the 2026 file holds nearly 180 million records in 208 GB of compressed JSONL across 35909 files, free over Academic Torrents; the REST API with update-date or index-date filters, rows=1000 and a cursor brings a copy current between releases.

limits.value: public pool: 5 requests a second for a single record, 1 a second for lists of records; concurrency 1
polite pool (email in mailto or the agent header): 10 requests a second for a single DOI record, 3 a second for lists; concurrency 3
Metadata Plus: 150 requests a second, no concurrency limit; annual subscription from USD 550
rows maximum 1000 per call; cursor paging beyond

record.binding_note: One list call a second anonymously, or 3 in the polite pool, makes a full harvest through the API slow; the annual file is the route to the whole registry.

identity_cost.detail: No signup or registration. An email address in the mailto parameter or the agent header selects the polite pool with higher limits. Metadata Plus is an annual subscription that issues an API key.

record.reliability_note: Over the limit answers 429; a manual block answers 403 and is lifted through support. The public and polite limits were revised from 1 December 2025.
record.confidence_note: The pool limits, the bulk file and its size are vendor pages read on 2026-10-30; two anonymous calls the same day returned the public-pool limits in their headers (1 a second for a list, 5 for a single DOI). The torrent was not downloaded.

free_tier.stated: No sign-up: the public pool allows 5 requests a second for a single record and 1 a second for lists of records, 1 at a time; the polite pool, selected by an email address in the mailto parameter or the agent header, allows 10 a second for a single DOI record and 3 a second for lists, 3 at a time; no daily cap is published
free_tier.notes: The limits come back in the x-rate-limit-limit, x-rate-limit-interval and x-concurrency-limit response headers; an anonymous list call on 2026-10-31 answered x-rate-limit-limit 1, x-rate-limit-interval 1s and x-concurrency-limit 1 in pool public-array.

per_object_cap.stated: rows maximum 1000 per call; rows=1000 with a five-field select returned 773,304 bytes in one response on 2026-10-31

retention.stated: A registered DOI cannot be fully deleted and its metadata can be updated, so a record is corrected rather than removed.
retention.notes: After a member cancels, its registered DOIs continue to exist and to resolve, and the metadata stays open through the APIs. The member can no longer update the metadata.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. No key, no account, no allowance published.

record.interface_detail: GET https://api.crossref.org/works with rows, cursor and select; content negotiation for single records. The polite pool is signalled with mailto= or a User-Agent carrying an address.
record.tooling: curl/python-requests; the harvester package and the documented cursor pattern. No SDK required.
record.chaining: Crossref supplies the DOI-level citation graph and licence metadata; the full text behind each DOI is a separate fetch from the publisher or from an OA mirror such as PMC or Europe PMC.

limits.value: public pool: 5 requests a second for a single record, 1 a second for lists of records, concurrency 1; polite pool (an email address in mailto or the agent header): 10 a second for a single DOI record, 3 a second for lists, concurrency 3
rows maximum 1000 per call, cursor paging beyond; rows=1000 with a five-field select returned 773,304 bytes on 2026-10-31

record.limits_note: Monthly snapshots are a Metadata Plus benefit fetched with a Crossref-Plus-API-Token header; the free bulk path is the annual public data file over Academic Torrents. Without a token, a HEAD of the documented URL https://api.crossref.org/snapshots/monthly/latest/all.json.tar.gz answered 200 with a zero-byte text/html body on 2026-10-31.
record.binding_note: One list call a second in the public pool, or 3 in the polite pool, each of at most 1000 rows, decides how many records a day the API yields; the annual public data file is the route to the whole registry.

identity_cost.detail: No signup or registration. An email address in the mailto parameter or the agent header selects the polite pool with higher limits; it is not a credential. Metadata Plus is an annual subscription that issues an API key.

record.reliability_note: Over the rate limit answers 429; a manual block answers 403 and is lifted through support. Without a Metadata Plus token the monthly snapshot URLs answer 200 with an empty or stub HTML body instead of an error, so a client must check the bytes it saves.
record.confidence_note: The pool limits are vendor pages read on 2026-10-31; an anonymous list call and an anonymous single-DOI call the same day returned the public-pool limits in their headers, and a rows=1000 call returned 773,304 bytes. The published limits were not tested at their ceiling.
